CIVIL REVISION PETITION NO: 1684/2023

Between:
Kota Chinna Venkata Subbarayudu and Others ...PETITIONER(S)
 AND Kota Venkata Ramanaiah and Others ...RESPONDENT(S)
Counsel for the Petitioner(S):
1. V NITESH Counsel for the Respondent(S):
1. P VENKATA RAMA SARMA
2 . M DELHI BABU

The Court made the following:
 THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE NYAPATHY VIJAY  C.R.P.No.1684 of 2023 ORDER :
Present Civil Revision Petition is filed challenging the order dated 06.05.2023 in I.A.No.472 of 2023 in O.S.No.104 of 2014 passed by the learned II Additional District Judge, Proddatur.
The petitioners herein are the defendants 5 to 9 in the Suit.
Respondent No.1 is the plaintiff and respondents 2 to 15 are the other defendants in the Suit.
2. Originally The Suit in O.S.No.104 of 2014 for Partition, was filed by the respondent No.1 herein.

While the Suit was at the stage of recording evidence, the petitioners filed a petition in I.A.No.472 of 2023 under Or.VIII R.1(A) of C.P.C. seeking to grant leave to the petitioners to file the documents Kota Chinna Venkata Subbarayudu vs Kota Venkata Ramanaiah on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51549197/
1 i.e., 1) Endorsement issued by the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition dated 16.12.2022 under Right to Information Act, 2) True copy of award No.8/1975 dated 13.03.1975 and 3) True copy of acknowledgment of receipt of compensation by my father Kota Subbarayudu under serial No.35,
on the ground that those documents were procured by the defendants recently.
This application was opposed by the respondents 2 to 5/ defendants 1 to 4.
The Trial Court dismissed the application, on the ground that no proper explanation was assigned for non-filing of proposed documents along with written statement or after framing of issues.
Hence, the present C.R.P. is filed.

3. Heard Sri V. Nitesh, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri P.Venkata Rama Sarma, larned counsel for the 1st respondent and Sri M.Delhi Babu, learned counsel for the respondents 2 to 5.
4.
The Suit is at the stage of evidence of defendants No.5 to 9 and the documents which are sought to be marked are the proceedings under Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

It would be in the interest of justice, if these documents are received in evidence, there may not be any serious dispute with regard to their genuineness and no prejudice would be caused to the other side.
Apart from that the petitioner had given reasonable explanation that those documents were received recently.

5. In the similar circumstances, in a decision between Sugandhi (Dead) by L.Rs. and Ors. Vs.
P.Rajkumar1

entities.text:
Sugandhi (Dead) by L.Rs. and Ors. Vs.
P.Rajkumar1

sentences.text:
, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:
"9.
It is often said that procedure is the handmaid of justice.
Procedural and technical hurdles shall not be allowed to come in the way of the court while doing substantial justice.
If the procedural violation does not seriously cause prejudice to the adversary party, courts must lean towards doing substantial justice rather than relying upon procedural and technical violation.

We should not forget the fact that litigation is nothing but a journey towards truth which is the foundation of justice and the court is required to Manu/SC/0792/2020 take appropriate steps to thrash out the underlying truth in every dispute.

Therefore, the court should take a lenient view when an application is made for production of the documents under subrule (3)."
6.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the impugned order of the Trial Court cannot be sustained and the same is liable to be set aside.

7. Accordingly, the Civil Revision Petition is allowed by setting aside the order dated 06.05.2023 in I.A.No.472 of 2023 in O.S.No.104 of 2014 passed by the learned II Additional District Judge,
Proddatur.
As a sequel, pending applications, if any, shall stand closed.
